This screen imports and stores your OpenVPN (.ovpn) and WireGuard (.conf) config files and lets you pick one as active. It does not yet establish a tunnel through them - that needs the official OpenVPN/WireGuard client engines integrated, which is a separate, larger piece of work. No server list is bundled: only servers you provide, from a source you trust, ever get added here.

NetShield can\'t connect to proxy servers itself. Save your provider\'s subscription URL here and send it to v2rayNG in one tap. The URL stays on this device, is never fetched or logged by NetShield, is hidden in this list and is excluded from backups.

v2rayNG isn\'t installed. Copy the URL and import it in your proxy app instead.

Android lets only one app hold the VPN at a time, so NetShield's VPN mode can't run together with another VPN or proxy app such as v2rayNG (for example with a Xeovo subscription).

To use both:
1. In NetShield, choose Local server mode and start it. It answers DNS at %1$s.
2. In your VPN or proxy app, set its DNS server to 127.0.0.1 on that port, and make sure DNS to 127.0.0.1 is sent directly, not through the proxy.

Some apps only accept DNS on port 53, which Android does not let NetShield use, so they cannot point at it. The name and place of that setting differ between apps and versions, and this has not been tested with every client.
Starting NetShield\'s VPN mode will disconnect it, because Android allows only one VPN at a time. To keep it connected, run NetShield in Local server mode instead.
Already use a proxy app such as v2rayNG (for example with a Xeovo subscription), Orbot or InviZible? NetShield can send your internet through it and still block ads and trackers.
Android allows only one VPN at a time, and NetShield has to be that VPN. So your proxy app must run WITHOUT its own VPN mode, as a plain proxy. Follow the steps for your app:

Good to know:
• While the proxy is on, your apps' internet goes through it. If the proxy app stops, the internet pauses until you start it again or switch this off.
• Video calls and games that use UDP may not work.
• Your home network (printers, TV casting) keeps working normally.
• DNS lookups also go through the proxy, so your provider can't see which sites you visit.

1. Open v2rayNG and add your server. For a Xeovo subscription, save its URL with the button below and open it in v2rayNG.
2. Open v2rayNG's Settings and set "Mode" to "Proxy only" (not "VPN"). Some versions show this in the side menu.
3. Pick your server and tap the connect button.
4. Check that no key icon is showing in your phone's status bar. A key means v2rayNG is still in VPN mode: go back to step 2.
5. Come back here and tap "Test connection".

In proxy-only mode v2rayNG listens on port 10808.

1. Open Orbot.
2. First time only: open Orbot's Settings and switch on "Power User Mode". This lets Orbot run without its own VPN.
3. Go back to Orbot's main screen and tap Start. Wait until Tor says it is connected.
4. Check that no key icon is showing in your phone's status bar. A key means a VPN is still running (a red warning will appear below if so).
5. Come back here and tap "Test connection".

Orbot shows its port number on the main screen. If it isn't 9050, enter that number under Advanced settings.

1. Open InviZible and switch it to "Proxy mode" in its settings (look for the operation or run mode). This lets it run without its own VPN.
2. Go back to the main screen and start Tor.
3. Check that no key icon is showing in your phone's status bar.
4. Come back here and tap "Test connection".

Menu names can differ between InviZible versions. Tor's port is usually 9050; if InviZible shows another number, enter it under Advanced settings.

What this tab can and can\'t do

Android does not let a normal installed app turn the system hotspot on/off, list or kick specific hotspot clients, or measure a device\'s data usage in MB/GB - those need system-level permissions this app can\'t have. What IS real here: any device that sets this phone as its DNS server (Wi-Fi or hotspot) gets the same block/allow lists as this phone, and this screen can block or daily-limit that device\'s DNS queries specifically.
On another device connected to this phone\'s Wi-Fi/hotspot, set its DNS server to this address to filter it with the same rules as this phone.

A domain or app on this list gets a full, unconditional bypass of every check this app makes: the sinkhole blocklist, per-device hotspot blocks, and query limits. Nothing here is hidden - everything you add or remove is exactly what\'s shown here. "psbdx.com" is pre-added because the app\'s own update checker depends on reaching it (blocking it would prevent update/security-fix notifications), and you can remove it like anything else. Per-app trusted status requires Android 10+ and VPN mode - it can\'t be determined in Local Server Mode or on older Android, and silently has no effect there rather than guessing.

NetShield is a private DNS resolver and ad and tracker blocker that runs on your phone, with a live dashboard of what your apps look up.\n\nNo account, no tracking, no Google services. This short setup takes about a minute and you can change everything later in Settings.

NetShield uses Android\'s VPN feature only to catch DNS lookups on your own phone and answer them locally. It is not a VPN service: your traffic is not sent to any NetShield server.\n\nAndroid asks you to confirm this once. You can do it now, or the first time you turn protection on.
Not allowed yet. You will be asked again when you turn protection on.
While protection is on, Android shows a small notification with the live status and a Stop button. Allowing notifications also lets you see if the protection ever stops unexpectedly.
This Android version does not need a separate permission.
This is where NetShield sends the lookups it does not block. You can change it any time in Settings.
Keep it running in the background
Some phones stop background apps to save battery, which would switch protection off. For reliable protection, turn off battery optimization for NetShield, or set its battery usage to Unrestricted.
Battery optimization is currently ON for NetShield.

Open the Dashboard and tap the big button to turn protection on.\n\nProxy mode, app routing (which apps use NetShield), blocklists and rules are in Settings.
